260	Rabbeinu says, that is true,
261	but don't think that it brings it closer in the sense that you can
262	stamp it and it is due to you. If you get into the corner
263	of "it is due to me, I did what I had to do," then you are
264	in trouble. Even great tzaddikim,
265	when they came to the Holy One, blessed be He, and said "it is due to me," were
266	put into a bad corner. Because if you are examined
267	by strict law, you will not come out, you will not come out of it well.
268	Chizkiyahu the king, our Sages say, was fit to be
269	Mashiach, we mentioned this several times, he was fit
270	to be Mashiach, and he said to the Holy One, blessed be He,
271	the following sentence, which none of us can say.
272	He could say it, and he said
273	it: "Remember now, Master of the world," I ask for salvation,
274	I ask that You hear my prayer. In the merit of what?
275	You should accept my prayer. Why?
276	"Remember now how I have walked before You in truth
277	and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." My heart
278	was pure, my deeds perfect, I ask
279	for something in return, I ask that my prayers be accepted. And then
280	the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, I will give you what
281	you asked,
282	in the merit of David My servant. In the merit of David My servant. Why? Because
283	if we enter that corner of what is due
284	to you, the attribute of din will not find you innocent. Do not
285	go in there. So even when you do what you do,
286	do not enter a kind of feeling of: now
287	it is truly due to me because I am a tzaddik. Beware of this
288	feeling. So here we see that again, on one
289	hand I need to act and do, because by strict law
290	the Redemption, the rectification, and the salvation, and a person's private salvation,
291	depend on his good deeds. On the other hand,
292	it is worthwhile to remember that everything is by chesed. Because if I
293	hang everything only on din, then I strengthen
294	the din. I arouse the din. And if on the other hand I
295	think that everything is only chesed, I also will not do
296	anything.
297	This is indeed what Rabbi Natan tells us in Likutei Halachot,
298	that Avraham
299	is chesed, and waste of chesed came out of him. What is
300	the waste of chesed? Yishmael, entirely waste, as
301	we see.
302	Esav is din, gevurah.
303	He came out of Yitzchak, who is din. Esav is the waste of
304	gevurah, waste of din, says Rabbi Natan. There is
305	in the heart of each one of us an Esav and a Yishmael.
306	What does Yishmael tell us in the heart? Everything is chesed, everything, everything,
307	everyone is on a high level, everything is good, bottom line, don't

309	wow, you seduced me now, you took me to a false chesed,

312	HaShem loves me anyway, right? He loves me, but
313	there is din, so I am required to act and do and rectify.
314	What does Esav say to a person in the heart? Din, according to
315	your deeds, according to how you behaved.
316	You are very, very far, and nothing is due to you,

354	Avinu, head of the believers, who taught his children that the way of
